notes: This source/test traceability contract covers the ownership boundary for explicit object-attribute update-region associations in Umbra's opt-in, non-installable IEEE 1516.1-2025 development profile. The private registry treats an update-region association as state of the current owner: when ownership is transferred, divested, unconditionally released, unpublished, or otherwise lost, the former association is erased and is not inherited by a later owner. The linked Catch2 scenario exercises If Available acquisition followed by Divestiture If Wanted and proves that a stale former-owner association cannot route an update until the new owner explicitly associates a region. Confirm Divestiture, unconditional divestiture, unpublish, and resignation use the same helper but remain implementation paths without separate public scenarios here. Default-region synthesis, scope-advisory callback completeness, regional request forms, negotiated ownership, save/restore, remote transport, package evidence, protected review, and conformance remain outside this slice.
